note: The refuter contract omitted the by-product section the review playbook required, so unrelated discoveries were discarded.
The portability rule relied on a false claim about this repository's remote and branch and did not explain the delayed failure mode.
The before-shot recipe hard-coded a remote and branch even though the playbook forbids both.
The handoff pointed bug fixing at an obsolete router section instead of the bundled bug-fixing playbook.
The plan exception sent failing work to an obsolete router section instead of the bundled bug-fixing playbook.
The help command used a fixed line range that leaked executable code and went stale whenever the header changed.
The audit assumed BSD stat and date flags, making the date calculation silently wrong on GNU systems.
The later audit path bypassed the new platform adapters and continued calling BSD-only commands directly.
The graph delegated to an undefined system, advertised the wrong retry cap, and put role selection in the wrong source of truth.
The review playbook named the drift tool as an internal script instead of its checked public command.
The review playbook required refuter by-products without ensuring that the refuter's output contract contained them.
The drift script's explanation claimed timestamps came from git even though its data came from the API.
The query omitted the total commit count, so it could not detect when its 250-commit window was truncated.
The drift calculation did not measure how many old commits the query had omitted.
A truncated commit list silently omitted the comparison base instead of warning that the result could not be pinned.
